scopeClaim.statement: Assessment is limited to the single declared expanded obligation and the two supplied fixed source crops; source discovery is not-tested, so this is not a repository-wide or all-entry claim.

results.explanation:
The fixed source establishes an application-level trusted-header capability but does not decide the actual deployment question. The POST /signin entry first rejects the request when password authentication is disabled, then requires the configured trusted-email header, lowercases its value, and uses that value as the email supplied to user lookup, optional provisioning, and email authentication. If authentication yields a user, the code returns a session response for that user. Thus a client-controlled header could select the identity at the application boundary only if the header is configured and the client can reach an ingress where its value is accepted; those deployment facts are expressly absent. The accepted policy denies this capability unless a trusted reverse proxy is the sole reachable ingress, removes client-supplied identity headers, and injects the authenticated identity. The source crops do not show whether those controls hold, so neither policy failure nor policy enforcement is source-decidable.

Public-question coverage: (1) The visible gates are ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH, configured WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER, presence of that header, and a successful email authentication; the selected-user session effect is reached only through the truthy-user branch. (2) The request header value is lowercased and assigned to email, which is passed to authenticate_user_by_email. (3) A truthy returned user is passed to create_session_response, binding the session to that selected user; the source does not expose the internals of that session creation. (4) The strongest accepted authorization control is the trusted-proxy policy's sole-ingress, stripping, and authenticated-replacement requirement, while the application-visible controls are the password-authentication and configured-header gates; the proxy controls are not present in the fixed context. (5) The protected effect is create_session_response for the authenticated user. (6) ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH, the configured trusted-header name, actual ingress reachability and client header control, proxy stripping/replacement behavior, and the authentication/database outcome can change the deployment answer; these observations are not supplied. (7) Before authentication, if lookup finds no user, the optional signup_handler is invoked with the header-selected email and name, so the branch can provision that identity before authenticate_user_by_email; this affects whether the selected identity is newly provisioned or already existing, but does not remove the need for successful authentication before session creation.
decisiveMissingFacts: The deployed ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH value; minimum observation: inspect the effective runtime configuration and establish whether it is true.
The deployed WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER value; minimum observation: inspect the effective runtime configuration and establish the exact header name or that it is unset.

Whether the unauthenticated external client can reach POST /signin through an ingress that forwards a client-controlled value for that configured header; minimum observation: verify the reachable request path and whether the test client can set the header at that ingress.

Whether the trusted reverse proxy is the sole reachable ingress and strips any client-supplied trusted identity header before injecting its own authenticated identity; minimum observation: inspect or test the effective proxy routing and header rewrite behavior, including direct-backend reachability.

Whether the supplied email is found or provisioned and whether authenticate_user_by_email returns a user in the deployment; minimum observation: observe the relevant database/authentication result for the supplied header value.
suggestedObservations: Read the effective ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH and trusted-header environment values.
Verify all reachable ingress paths and direct backend exposure for POST /signin.
Verify proxy removal and authenticated replacement of the trusted-email header.
Observe whether authenticate_user_by_email returns a user and whether create_session_response is reached for the selected identity.

entry.statement: The declared entry is POST /signin, and the signin handler contains the trusted-header branch.

binding.statement: When the trusted-email header is configured and present, its request value is lowercased and assigned to email; that email is used for lookup, optional signup, and email authentication.

If no user is found, signup_handler is called with the header-selected email and name before email authentication, so the optional provisioning branch can create the selected identity before authentication.

resource.statement: After authenticate_user_by_email returns a truthy user, the handler passes that user to create_session_response, which is the source-visible binding of the selected identity to the returned session response.

control.statement: Application processing is gated by ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH; when false, the handler raises a forbidden error before the trusted-header branch.
The trusted-header branch is enabled only when WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER is configured, and it rejects a request lacking that header.

The accepted policy requires sole trusted-proxy ingress, removal of client-supplied identity headers, and injection of the authenticated identity; those deployment controls are not represented in the supplied application crops.

effect.statement: The protected session effect occurs only when user is truthy; then create_session_response is called with that user and set_cookie=True, otherwise an invalid-credentials error is raised.
Successful authentication may also apply trusted group and role header values to the selected user before session creation when those optional headers are configured and supplied.

condition.statement: Password authentication must be enabled before any trusted-header processing can occur.
The trusted-email header name is environment-controlled, and the branch requires both a configured name and a corresponding request header.
The session path requires authenticate_user_by_email to yield a user.

The actual deployment values, ingress reachability, proxy header handling, and authentication outcome are not supplied by the fixed source context, so the policy disposition for the real deployment remains unknown.
